key_insight: RollVerify keeps the efficiency of partial-rollout RL while recovering on-policy-like accuracy by verifying and repairing long-tail trajectories before training.
engineering_relevance: It addresses a systems bottleneck in long-context RL for LLM reasoning, reducing GPU bubbles and training cost without sacrificing final model quality.
method: Defines an off-policy shift metric (OPS) to measure how far partial rollouts drift from on-policy behavior.
Uses OPS-guided sequence-level and token-level verification to detect invalid suffixes in trajectories.
Truncates or repairs low-quality tail segments before samples enter training.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that experiments on mathematical and tool-assisted mathematical reasoning match on-policy accuracy while lowering training cost, with additional code-generation results suggesting broader applicability.
watch_item: OPS thresholds and verification rules may be sensitive to rollout distribution shifts, so the method could require careful tuning to avoid discarding useful long-tail reasoning.
paper_title: RollVerify: Bridging Efficiency and Accuracy in Long-Tail Rollout Reinforcement Learning
